title: Salmon with Miso Butter
subtitle: Baked salmon fillets with a white miso and honey glaze
excerpt: A compound butter of white miso, honey, and ginger melts over the salmon as it bakes, forming a rich, savoury glaze. It is an exceptionally quick and impressive dinner. The miso butter can be made well in advance.
sourceNotes: Based on Japanese miso-glazed fish technique. White miso is milder and sweeter than red, making it well-suited to fish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roll the miso butter in cling film and refrigerate for up to 5 days, or freeze for 1 month.

content.text: Make the miso butter first. It needs 30 minutes in the fridge to firm up enough to slice. If you are in a rush, put it in the freezer for 10 minutes instead.
Beat the softened butter, miso, honey, grated ginger, and soy sauce together in a bowl until smooth.
Spoon the butter onto a sheet of cling film. Roll into a log shape. Twist the ends to seal. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line the baking tray with foil.
Place the salmon fillets skin-side down on the tray. Season lightly.
Slice the miso butter into 8 rounds. Place 2 rounds on top of each fillet.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the salmon is cooked through and the butter has melted into a glaze.
Scatter with spring onion. Serve with steamed rice and green vegetables.

items.symptom: Miso butter slides off the salmon
items.cause: Butter not chilled enough before slicing
items.fix: Chill for the full 30 minutes until firm.
Check at 12 minutes; it should flake easily at the thickest point.

items.symptom: Glaze burns before salmon is cooked
items.fix: Reduce to 180C and cover loosely with foil for the last 5 minutes.
